subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these goal records.

judge.implied_focus: The nature and substance of each goal — what it aims to improve, how, at what scope, and how well-specified/actionable it is — i.e., characterizing goals to identify which merit attention.

per_column.name: goal_outcome_domain
per_column.rationale: Classifies the substantive outcome area of the goal, a core facet of what the goal is about.

per_column.name: improvement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Captures the 'how' — the lever used to achieve the goal, a coherent facet of goal substance.

per_column.name: targeted_improvement_scope
per_column.rationale: Identifies the specific object being improved; complements outcome domain, though partially redundant with it (parallel value counts).

per_column.name: implementation_timeline_clarity
per_column.rationale: Measures specificity of timing, a well-specification facet relevant to whether a goal is actionable/worth attention.

per_column.name: financial_impact_quantified
per_column.rationale: Flags whether financial impact is quantified — a facet of goal rigor/attention-worthiness.

per_column.name: goal_scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: Distinguishes single-function vs enterprise-wide reach, a meaningful facet of goal significance.

per_column.name: execution_complexity_estimate
per_column.rationale: Estimates difficulty of execution, directly relevant to what merits attention and risk.

judge.rationale: The columns cohere around a single inferable focus: characterizing the substance and attention-worthiness of each goal. They form a sound multi-faceted structure spanning what (outcome domain, targeted scope), how (mechanism), significance (scope breadth), rigor/specification (timeline clarity, financial quantification), and effort/risk (complexity). This is neither a single restatement nor generic noise, and the facets are data-inferable from description/dates/metric fields. Minor deductions: goal_outcome_domain and targeted_improvement_scope are near-duplicates (identical observed counts suggest parallel derivation, weakening differentiation), and execution_complexity_estimate is a somewhat coarse/derived judgment. The implied focus is genuinely actionable — an analyst could triage goals by significance, rigor, and complexity to decide what merits attention.
